# common

## What this is
**Id:** blk-c218b0b8e576

common is oni-mods-common (`https://github.com/isochronous/oni-mods-common`), the shared build configuration and tooling of the isochronous Oxygen Not Included mods, included in the ONI-Mods monorepo as the `common/` submodule. Every mod csproj imports `oni-mod.props` and `oni-mod.targets` through `$(OniCommon)`, which ONI-Mods sets in its `Directory.Build.props`, so the target framework, the game assembly references, game folder detection and the deploy-to-local-mods step change in one place after a game update. It also holds the translation loader compiled into mods that set `UseTranslations`, and the tools that make art and previews, check, test, release and publish the mods. The mod author uses it every time a mod in `mods/` is built, tested or released.

## Where things are
**Id:** blk-0aca56964b6a

Top-level folders and key files:

- `oni-mod.props`: imported at the top of a mod csproj. net48, C# 9, the game folder (`GameFolder`, `GameLibsFolder`, the `ONI_GAME_FOLDER` environment variable, then the known Steam folders) and `ModDeployFolder`.
- `oni-mod.targets`: imported at the bottom of a mod csproj. The game assembly references, the opt-in `ReferenceUnityUI`, `ReferenceImageConversion`, `UsePLib` and `UseTranslations` extras, the `EnsureGameLibs` check and the `DeployToLocalMods` step.
- `ilrepack-plib.targets`: the `MergePLib` target that merges PLib into the mod DLL when `UsePLib` is set, wired in by `oni-mod.targets` as `ILRepackTargetsFile`.
- `src/Translations.cs`: `Isochronous.Translations`, which registers a mod's `ModStrings` tree and applies its `translations/<locale>.po` files; compiled into mods that set `UseTranslations`.
- `tools/`: the shared tools (Kanim, MakePreview, ModCheck, ModTest, Release, SaveRunner, TestRunner, Translations, WorkshopUpload, WorldgenDriver) and `requirements.txt` for the Python ones. It is this node's one child node.
- `README.md`: using common in a mod, the build knobs, what to do after a game update, translations, releases, Workshop publishing, previews, kanims, testing a mod in isolation and reproducing a report in a save.
- `.gitignore`: build output (`bin/`, `obj/`), the `runs/` folders of WorldgenDriver, SaveRunner and TestRunner, and the Graystroke font.
- `.gitattributes`: line-ending and merge rules for the `.context/` files.

The `.context/` documents of this node: `decisions/`, `retrospectives/`, and `projects.md`, which lists the child node `tools`.

# tools

## What this is
**Id:** blk-647210c6a78a

`tools/` holds the command-line tools and development mods shared by every isochronous Oxygen Not Included mod: making kanims and Workshop previews, checking a mod DLL against the game, testing a mod alone or through its in-game tests, reproducing a report in a save or a worldgen, writing translation templates, and cutting releases to GitHub and the Steam Workshop. The mod author runs them from the ONI-Mods root or a mod's folder. Some call others: `Release/release.py` uploads through `WorkshopUpload`, `TestRunner/Invoke-OniTests.ps1` runs `ModCheck`, and `Translations/translations.py` runs `StringsTemplate`.

## Where things are
**Id:** blk-6c2bbf052519

Folders and key files:

- `Kanim/`: `kanim.py` reads, writes, renders and extracts Klei kanims, from the command line or imported by a mod's art script.
- `MakePreview/`: `make_preview.py` composes the 256x256 sprite-and-caption Workshop preview; `title_preview.py` makes the 512x512 preview with the mod's title over a background; `fonts/` holds the fonts they use.
- `ModCheck/`: a .NET 8 console tool that loads a mod DLL against the game assemblies and reports type-load and missing-member failures without launching the game.
- `ModTest/`: `Test-OniMods.ps1` launches the game with only the mods under development enabled and restores `mods.json` afterwards; `disabled.txt` and `included.txt` adjust the default loadout.
- `Release/`: `release.py` builds, packages, tags and publishes one mod to GitHub and the Workshop; `release_mods.py` releases every mod that changed since its last release.
- `SaveRunner/`: a dev mod plus `Invoke-SaveRun.ps1` that load a save unattended with saving blocked, record a probe once per game second and quit.
- `TestRunner/`: a dev mod plus `Invoke-OniTests.ps1` that run a mod's `[OniTest]` in-game tests unattended in the real game.
- `Translations/`: `translations.py` rewrites each mod's `.pot` template from its built DLL and checks its `.po` files; `StringsTemplate/` is the .NET 8 program it runs for that.
- `WorkshopUpload/`: the legacy-API Steam Workshop publisher, run as Klei's Oxygen Not Included Uploader (app 636750).
- `WorldgenDriver/`: a dev mod plus `Invoke-Worldgen.ps1` that generate clusters in the real game unattended for a list of coordinates and write one result per coordinate.
- `requirements.txt`: the Python packages the Python tools need (Pillow, numpy, scipy, UnityPy).
- `.gitattributes`: line-ending and merge rules for the `.context/` files below.

Six folders are nodes with their own `.context/`: `ModCheck`, `SaveRunner`, `TestRunner`, `Translations/StringsTemplate`, `WorkshopUpload` and `WorldgenDriver`; `projects.md` lists them. `Kanim`, `MakePreview`, `ModTest`, `Release` and `Translations/translations.py` have none.

The `.context/` documents of this node: `decisions/` and `projects.md`.

# ModCheck domain

## Overview
**Id:** blk-303b29f17bb1

ModCheck loads one mod DLL against the real game assemblies on a .NET 8 host and checks, without launching the game, the two ways a mod dies after a game update: a type that cannot be set up, and a call to a member that no longer exists. It is a console program, `common/tools/ModCheck`, built and run with `dotnet run`. `common/tools/TestRunner/Invoke-OniTests.ps1` runs it on every test DLL before a game session; a mod author runs it by hand after a game update.

## Key Entities
**Id:** blk-dda267d443bd

### Program
**Id:** blk-051b98125fc9  
**Description**: the whole tool: argument handling, assembly resolution, the type and method loops and the exit code.  
**Location**: `Program.cs`

| Member | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `Main(string[] args)` | entry point; returns the exit code |
| `Report(stage, typeName, memberName, ex, ref failures, ref warnings)` | classifies one exception as `FAIL` or `WARN` and prints it |
| `AllMethods(type, flags)` | the type's methods and constructors in one array |
| `Unwrap(ex)` | `ExceptionType: message`, seen through `TypeInitializationException` |

**Relationships**: reads the game's Managed folder (first argument) and the mod DLL (second); writes only to standard output and the exit code.

### The two checks
**Id:** blk-6fe7024707c2

1. **Type load**: for each type in the assembly, `GetInterfaceMap` for every interface of a non-interface type, then `RuntimeHelpers.RunClassConstructor`. Catches `VTable setup of type X failed` and failing static constructors.
2. **JIT**: for each non-abstract method and constructor with no open generic parameters, declared on the type (public and non-public, instance and static), `RuntimeHelpers.PrepareMethod`. Compiling the body resolves every member it references, so a missing method or field fails here instead of at call time in the game.

### Inputs
**Id:** blk-ff7f3244936c

| Input | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| game Managed directory | `OxygenNotIncluded_Data\Managed` of the installed game; `Assembly-CSharp`, `0Harmony`, Unity modules and the rest resolve from here |
| mod DLL | the assembly under test; its own dependencies are resolved from the same Managed folder, so a DLL with others (TestRunner, the mod under test) is checked from a folder that holds them (see `Invoke-OniTests.ps1`) |

### Output
**Id:** blk-c3c2239a19af

Lines on standard output (see [error handling](../standards/error-handling.md)) and an exit code of 0, 1 or 2.

## Business Rules
**Id:** blk-1031f9e9f9e0

- Every type is checked even after a failure; every method of a type that loaded is checked.
- A message containing `ECall methods must be packaged into a system module` is a warning: the host cannot run Unity native code that the game runs. Everything else is a failure.
- `BeginInvoke` and `EndInvoke` of delegate types are not compiled; abstract methods and open generic methods are not compiled.
- ModCheck runs on .NET 8 or later. The desktop CLR rejects the game's default interface methods.
- A pass says nothing about behaviour at run time; it covers type setup and member resolution only.

## Domain Terminology
**Id:** blk-732559c369a5

| Term | Definition |
|------|-----------|
| Managed directory | the folder of the game's .NET assemblies |
| JIT check | forcing compilation of a method body with `PrepareMethod` |
| Type check | touching a type's interface maps and static constructor |

## Key Code Paths
**Id:** blk-9a1ec07e6286

- **Whole run**: `Main` builds the resolver, loads the assembly, loops over `asm.GetTypes()` and prints the summary and exit code. See `Program.cs`.
- **One type**: the type stage in a `try`, then `AllMethods` and `PrepareMethod` per method, then `OK <type>`. See `Program.cs`.
- **Classification**: `Report` decides `FAIL` or `WARN` from the unwrapped message. See `Program.cs`.
- **Caller in the repository**: the `dotnet run -c Release --project tools\ModCheck -- <managed> <dll>` line in `common/tools/TestRunner/Invoke-OniTests.ps1`, which exits 3 when ModCheck fails.

## Related
**Id:** blk-f3cc2c826e21

- See also: [glossary](glossary.md)
- Governed by: [naming conventions](../standards/naming-conventions.md)

# ModCheck glossary

Terms a newcomer to ModCheck needs. Entity detail is in [entities](entities.md).

## Abbreviations and Acronyms
**Id:** blk-3aa35e536ac3

| Abbreviation | Full Term | Context |
|--------------|-----------|---------|
| ONI | Oxygen Not Included | the game whose mods ModCheck checks |
| JIT | just-in-time compiler | `PrepareMethod` forces it to compile a method before the method runs |
| CLR | Common Language Runtime | the desktop (.NET Framework) runtime that ModCheck cannot use; CoreCLR is the .NET 8 one it does use |
| ECall | external call | a method implemented in the Unity engine's native code; the host cannot run it |
| DIM | default interface method | an interface method with a body; the game's interfaces have them |

## Cross-Domain Terms
**Id:** blk-497458e05560

### VTable setup failure
**Id:** blk-7d3bfdfef868

**Definition**: the runtime error `VTable setup of type X failed` raised when a type's virtual or interface methods cannot be laid out, which a game update causes by changing an interface or base class that the mod's type implements or derives from. `GetInterfaceMap` is how the check provokes it.  
**Used in**: ModCheck output (`FAIL type ...`).

### Missing member
**Id:** blk-cdaff890db76  
**Definition**: a `MissingMethodException` or `MissingFieldException`, raised when compiled code names a method or field that the game no longer has. Compiling every method body with `PrepareMethod` brings these out without calling the code.  
**Used in**: ModCheck output (`FAIL jit ...`).

### Managed directory
**Id:** blk-a6b4a8ed18b6  
**Definition**: the game's `OxygenNotIncluded_Data\Managed` folder, the first argument.  
**Used in**: ModCheck's `AssemblyResolve` handler; `Invoke-OniTests.ps1` finds it from the game folder.

### Warning
**Id:** blk-841800be19a4  
**Definition**: a `WARN` line for an exception caused by the check host and not by the mod (the `ECall` case); it does not fail the run.  
**Used in**: ModCheck output.

## Related
**Id:** blk-af856d8d8196

- See also: [entities](entities.md)

# Code Style Guide

## Formatting
**Id:** blk-59184ca785a3

ModCheck is one file, `Program.cs`, and one project file, `ModCheck.csproj`.

- Tabs, one per level, in `Program.cs`, the same as the mod sources. The csproj uses two spaces.
- Opening brace on its own line (Allman) for the class, methods and multi-line blocks. A body of one short statement goes on the next line without braces (`if (args.Length < 2)` and the `continue` guards in `Main`).
- No line length limit. Long conditions and calls wrap after an operator or argument with the continuation indented one tab (`const BindingFlags all = ...` in `Program.cs`).
- The repository has no `.editorconfig`. TODO(owner): decide whether to add one recording tabs and brace placement for all of `common/`.

## Language and Toolchain
**Id:** blk-3d0e75841249

- C# 9 (`LangVersion` 9.0) on .NET 8 (`TargetFramework` net8.0), `OutputType` Exe. The project does not import `common/oni-mod.props`: it is a console program, not a mod, and has no game references at build time.
- ModCheck must run on .NET 8 or later, never .NET Framework. The game's interfaces use default interface methods, which the desktop CLR rejects and CoreCLR accepts, as does the game's Mono runtime. The header comment of `Program.cs` says so; keep it when the file changes.
- No NuGet packages. The code uses only `System`, `System.IO`, `System.Reflection` and `System.Runtime.CompilerServices`.

## Imports
**Id:** blk-d831aad7e6ca

`using` directives sit at the top, alphabetical, with no blank lines between them (`System`, `System.IO`, `System.Reflection`, `System.Runtime.CompilerServices`). No aliases and no global usings.

## Structure
**Id:** blk-224789a75291

- A single `internal static class Program` holds `Main` and its private static helpers (`Report`, `AllMethods`, `Unwrap`). Helpers are `private static` and sit below `Main`.
- There are no instances and no shared state: the failure and warning counters are locals of `Main` passed to `Report` by `ref`.
- A new check goes in as another loop body in `Main` or another helper beside the existing ones, and reports through `Report` so the failure and warning counts stay accurate.

## Comments
**Id:** blk-9bbfb0a9ecda

- A block comment at the top of `Program.cs` says what the tool verifies, why it needs .NET 8, and the usage line. Update it with any behaviour change.
- Comments inside the code give the reason for a rule, which is the runtime difference between the check host (CoreCLR) and the game's Mono: why `BeginInvoke` and `EndInvoke` are skipped on delegates, why the `ECall` message is a warning. No comments that restate the code.
- Console strings are plain text; the summary line uses an em dash (`runtime-mismatch artifacts, fine in-game`).

## Related
**Id:** blk-a530d607ccfd

- See also: [error handling](error-handling.md)
- See also: [naming conventions](naming-conventions.md)

# Error Handling Conventions

## Principles
**Id:** blk-4aa5247ed7a4

1. **Report every break, not the first.** A check run lists every type and method that fails, so one run shows the whole damage after a game update. `Main` counts failures and warnings and keeps going.
2. **Name the member.** Each line names the stage, the type and, for a JIT failure, the method, with the exception type and message.
3. **Tell a real break from a host artifact.** The check host is CoreCLR with no Unity engine; the game is Mono with one. Only the failures that the game would also hit count.
4. **The exit code is the verdict.** Callers (`common/tools/TestRunner/Invoke-OniTests.ps1`) read the exit code, not the text.

## Exit Codes
**Id:** blk-615b71d8cae1

| Code | Meaning | Set in |
|------|---------|--------|
| 0 | every type loaded and every method compiled, warnings allowed | `Main`, `ALL CHECKS PASSED` |
| 1 | one or more failures | `Main`, `N FAILURE(S)` |
| 2 | wrong arguments, usage printed | `Main`, `args.Length < 2` |

The tool prints `usage: ModCheck <game Managed dir> <mod dll>` to standard output for exit code 2.

## Output Lines
**Id:** blk-635cd6eaebb7

Everything goes to standard output, one line per event, with a fixed prefix:

| Prefix | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `OK <type>` | the type stage passed (interface maps resolved, static constructor ran) and the method loop finished; `FAIL jit` lines for its methods print before it |
| `FAIL type <type>: ...` | type load, interface map or static constructor failure |
| `FAIL jit <type>.<method>: ...` | a method body could not be compiled; `PrepareMethod` threw, for example `MissingMethodException` or `MissingFieldException` for a member the game no longer has |
| `FAIL loader: <type> :: <message>` | one loader exception from a `ReflectionTypeLoadException` |
| `FAIL: <exception>` | any other exception while loading the assembly |
| `WARN <stage> <member>: ...` | a runtime-mismatch artifact, counted separately and not a failure |

## Handling Patterns
**Id:** blk-b80f483cffaf

### Per-type isolation
**Id:** blk-27d2629f8e78

The type stage and each method's JIT call are wrapped in their own `try`/`catch (Exception)` in `Main`. A failure goes to `Report`, the loop continues, and the type is not printed as `OK` when its type stage failed (`continue` after `Report`). The broad catch is the point of the tool: any exception from touching a type or method is a result to report.

### Loader exceptions
**Id:** blk-82f4670e9d62

`ReflectionTypeLoadException` from `asm.GetTypes()` is caught separately and every entry of `LoaderExceptions` becomes a `FAIL loader` line and a failure. Any other exception around the whole load becomes one `FAIL:` line with the full exception text.

### Host artifacts
**Id:** blk-00ca86cc07f8

`Report` treats an exception whose unwrapped message contains `ECall methods must be packaged into a system module` as a warning. That message means the host tried to run Unity native code, which works in the game. `MissingMethodException`, `MissingFieldException` and `TypeLoadException` are never downgraded. `BeginInvoke` and `EndInvoke` of delegates are not compiled at all, because their stubs throw `PlatformNotSupportedException` on CoreCLR and work on Mono. Abstract methods and methods with open generic parameters are skipped.

### Unwrapping
**Id:** blk-76c47a4d4fde

`Unwrap` follows `TypeInitializationException` to its inner exception, so a failing static constructor shows the cause and not the wrapper.

### Assembly resolution
**Id:** blk-534f0b7eade5

The `AssemblyResolve` handler looks for `<name>.dll` in the game's Managed folder and returns `null` when it is not there, which lets the runtime report the missing assembly in its own words.

## Anti-Patterns to Avoid
**Id:** blk-50d5a04f2f9a

- Stopping at the first failure; the count and the list are the output.
- Downgrading a failure to a warning without a runtime reason written next to the rule.
- Writing results to anything but standard output and the exit code; the callers capture both.

## Related
**Id:** blk-7f1a6895f34c

- See also: [code style](code-style.md)

# Naming Conventions

## Files and Directories
**Id:** blk-8ff7fead9871

- The tool lives in `common/tools/ModCheck`: `ModCheck.csproj` and `Program.cs`. The project, the assembly and the folder share the name `ModCheck`.
- The ICON store for the tool is `common/tools/ModCheck/.context`.
- Build output goes to `bin/` and `obj/` (ignored by `common/.gitignore`).

## Code Naming
**Id:** blk-aa161d844e40

- Types, methods and parameters follow C# convention: PascalCase for types and methods (`Program`, `Report`, `AllMethods`, `Unwrap`), camelCase for parameters and locals (`managedDir`, `modDll`, `isDelegate`, `failures`).
- Local constants are camelCase too (`const BindingFlags all`).
- Methods start with a verb or name what they return: `Report`, `AllMethods`, `Unwrap`.
- Counters are plural nouns (`failures`, `warnings`) passed by `ref`.
- No `I` interfaces and no type prefixes; there is one class.

## Command Line
**Id:** blk-6bdab3ca51dd

- Two positional arguments in a fixed order: the game's Managed directory, then the mod DLL. No options or flags.
- The mod DLL path is made absolute with `Path.GetFullPath` before use.

## Output Vocabulary
**Id:** blk-0902df8ac85c

- Stages in a result line are the lowercase words `type` and `jit`; the loader failure is `loader`.
- Line prefixes are upper case: `OK`, `FAIL`, `WARN`. The final lines are `ALL CHECKS PASSED` or `<n> FAILURE(S)`.
- Types are printed by `Type.FullName`, methods by `Name` after the type, as `Namespace.Type.Method`.

## Related
**Id:** blk-d692513e0e50

- See also: [code style](code-style.md)

# SaveRunner domain

## Overview
**Id:** blk-a0e41250aa34

SaveRunner loads a save in the real game with nobody at the keyboard, runs the colony for a number of game seconds with all saving blocked, records readings once per game second and quits. It exists to reproduce an in-game observation from a player's save, with and without a mod, under real sim behaviour and the player's own mod loadout. Two parts: a development mod (`SaveRunner`, inert unless the game starts with `--saverun=FILE`) and a launcher (`Invoke-SaveRun.ps1`). It is not published to the Workshop.

## Key Entities
**Id:** blk-6e0fb1c00ac7

### SaveRunnerMod
**Id:** blk-ca4d28981335  
**Description**: the mod's entry point (`UserMod2`). Reads the command line at load; when a run is on it sets the crash-reporter flags and installs quit tracing.  
**Location**: `Mod.cs`  
**Relationships**: calls `Runner.ReadCommandLine`; traces `App.Restart` and `Application.Quit` through `TracePatch`/`TraceQuit`; the Harmony patches in `Patches.cs` are applied by `base.OnLoad`.

### Runner
**Id:** blk-b5fe6721e0d5  
**Description**: the command line and state of one run, and the way it ends.  
**Location**: `Runner.cs`

| Member | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `Active` | true when `--saverun=FILE` was given |
| `SavePath`, `Seconds`, `Speed`, `Probe`, `OutFile`, `TimeoutSeconds` | the options |
| `Started`, `Finished` | load requested; run ended |
| `StartedAt`, `MenuSeenAt` | real-time marks (`MenuSeenAt` is -1 until the main menu appears) |
| `Finish(status, detail)` | writes the status line, quits |

### Patches
**Id:** blk-4905afd4b039  
**Description**: the Harmony patches, each a no-op unless `Runner.Active`.  
**Location**: `Patches.cs`

| Patch | Target | Does |
|-------|--------|------|
| `MainMenu_OnSpawn_Patch` | `MainMenu.OnSpawn` | notes when the menu appeared |
| `App_LateUpdate_Patch` | `App.LateUpdate` | four seconds after the menu: checks the file exists and calls `LoadScreen.DoLoad(path)`; also the real-time timeout watchdog |
| `Game_OnSpawn_Patch` | `Game.OnSpawn` | adds `RunBehaviour` to the Game object once the colony is up |
| `SaveLoader_Save_Patch` | `SaveLoader.Save(string, bool, bool)` | skips the save and returns the filename |
| `App_Quit_Patch` | `App.Quit` | logs who quit, with a stack when it was not the runner |

### RunBehaviour
**Id:** blk-1f9288a97c7a  
**Description**: a `MonoBehaviour` on the Game object for one run. Unpauses and sets the speed, accumulates scaled frame time as game seconds, samples the probe once per game second, ends the run at `Runner.Seconds`.  
**Location**: `RunBehaviour.cs`  
**Relationships**: owns the CSV `StreamWriter`; calls `FridgeProbe.Sample`; ends through `Runner.Finish`.

### FridgeProbe
**Id:** blk-043bf2a0945a  
**Description**: the one probe, `fridges`. For every building with a `RefrigeratorController.Def` and every item in its `Storage`, writes controller state, powered state, whether No Magic Fridges' `FridgeThermostat` is on the building, the def's setpoint, the cell's temperature, element and mass, and per item its element, mass, temperature, `SimTemperatureTransfer` surface area and ground-transfer scale, whether that component is enabled, its sim handle and `deltaKJ`.  
**Location**: `RunBehaviour.cs`

### Invoke-SaveRun.ps1
**Id:** blk-3eb75b734c83  
**Description**: the launcher. Copies the save into the run folder, rewrites `mods.json` for the run, starts the game through Steam, waits for it to quit, restores `mods.json`, prints the status.  
**Location**: `Invoke-SaveRun.ps1`

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `-Save` | the `.sav` to load (required) |
| `-Seconds`, `-Speed` | game seconds (default 60) and speed 1 to 3 |
| `-Probe` | `fridges` or none |
| `-With`, `-Without` | mods to add or remove for the run |
| `-TimeoutSec`, `-Label`, `-OutDir`, `-SteamExe`, `-AppId` | real-time limit (900), run-folder prefix, output root, Steam path, game app id (457140) |

### Files it reads and writes
**Id:** blk-2c721000393a

| File | Direction | Purpose |
|------|-----------|---------|
| the save | read | copied to `runs/<Label>-<stamp>/colony.sav`; the original is never opened by the game |
| `Documents\Klei\OxygenNotIncluded\mods\mods.json` | read, write, restored | the loadout: current mods, plus SaveRunner and `-With`, minus `-Without`; backup at `mods.json.saverun-backup` |
| `kplayerprefs.yaml` | read | tells whether the game is in Spaced Out mode so `enabledForDlc` is set to match |
| `probe.csv` | written by the game | one row per item per game second, or one row for an empty fridge; written only when `--saverun-probe` is given (the launcher always passes `--saverun-out`) |
| `probe.csv.status` | written by the game | one JSON line when the run ends |
| `Player.log` | copied | into the run folder after the game exits |

## Business Rules
**Id:** blk-ae74a2604bba

- Without `--saverun` the mod changes nothing.
- Nothing is saved while a run is on: `SaveLoader.Save` is skipped, and the game opens a copy of the save.
- The game's mode (base game or Spaced Out) is left as it is; the save has to be from the current mode.
- Mod Profile Manager (Workshop 2854869130) and its Light addon (3281716506) restart the game when a save loads with a different mod list, which a run always has; disable them with `-Without 2854869130,3281716506`.
- The save path travels through Steam's command line, so the copy is named `colony.sav` in a folder without spaces.
- The launcher refuses to start when the game is already running.

## Key Code Paths
**Id:** blk-d8b4ef45566a

- **Start**: `Invoke-SaveRun.ps1` builds the arguments and runs `steam.exe -applaunch 457140 --saverun=...`; the game loads the mod, `SaveRunnerMod.OnLoad` reads the arguments. See `Mod.cs`, `Runner.cs`.
- **Load**: `MainMenu.OnSpawn` postfix notes the time; the `App.LateUpdate` postfix calls `LoadScreen.DoLoad` four seconds later. See `Patches.cs`.
- **Run**: `Game.OnSpawn` postfix adds `RunBehaviour`; it samples each game second and finishes at the time limit. See `RunBehaviour.cs`.
- **End**: `Runner.Finish` writes the status line and quits; the launcher sees the process exit, copies `Player.log`, restores `mods.json`. See `Runner.cs`, `Invoke-SaveRun.ps1`.

## State Transitions
**Id:** blk-bafa30d4781e

| State | Transitions To | Trigger |
|-------|---------------|---------|
| inactive | waiting for menu | `--saverun` given |
| waiting for menu | loading | four seconds after the menu appeared (`Runner.Started`) |
| waiting for menu | finished (`no-save`) | file not found |
| loading | running | `Game.OnSpawn`, `RunBehaviour` added |
| running | finished (`done`) | game seconds reached |
| running | finished (`runner-error`) | exception in `RunBehaviour.Update` |
| waiting for menu, loading or running | finished (`timeout`) | real time since the command line was read passes `TimeoutSeconds` before the run finishes |

## Related
**Id:** blk-bf1ccef2e930

- See also: [glossary](glossary.md)
- Governed by: [naming conventions](../standards/naming-conventions.md)

# SaveRunner glossary

Terms a newcomer to SaveRunner needs. Entity detail is in [entities](entities.md).

## Abbreviations and Acronyms
**Id:** blk-bd9fd4d15776

| Abbreviation | Full Term | Context |
|--------------|-----------|---------|
| ONI | Oxygen Not Included | the game |
| SMI | state machine instance | `RefrigeratorController.StatesInstance`, read by the fridge probe |
| STT | `SimTemperatureTransfer` | the component that exchanges heat between an item and its cell; columns `surfaceArea`, `groundTransferScale`, `sttEnabled`, `simHandle`, `deltaKJ` |
| SO | Spaced Out | the expansion; the launcher reads it from `kplayerprefs.yaml` |
| NMF | No Magic Fridges | a mod whose `FridgeThermostat` the probe looks for |

## Cross-Domain Terms
**Id:** blk-cfb3406478e6

### Run
**Id:** blk-fca79a60d4bc  
**Definition**: one game launch by `Invoke-SaveRun.ps1`: load a save, play for `--saverun-seconds` game seconds, write the probe, quit. Its folder is `runs/<Label>-<stamp>`.  
**Used in**: the launcher, `Runner`, every file name under `runs/`.

### Probe
**Id:** blk-4e73227a1e2f  
**Definition**: a named recorder sampled once per game second during a run. `fridges` is the only one.  
**Used in**: `--saverun-probe`, `RunBehaviour`, `FridgeProbe`.

### Game seconds and real seconds
**Id:** blk-dd09f79f5775  
**Definition**: game seconds are scaled frame time (speed 3 passes three of them per real second); `--saverun-seconds` is in game seconds, `--saverun-timeout` in real seconds.  
**Used in**: `RunBehaviour.Update`, `App_LateUpdate_Patch`.

### Status file
**Id:** blk-67145d475ebb  
**Definition**: `<out>.status`, one JSON line (`done`, `timeout`, `no-save` or `runner-error`) that tells the launcher how the run ended.  
**Used in**: `Runner.Finish`, the launcher's final report.

### Loadout
**Id:** blk-e9f19f346fa7  
**Definition**: the list of enabled mods in `mods.json`. A run keeps the player's loadout, adds SaveRunner and `-With`, removes `-Without`, and puts the original back afterwards.  
**Used in**: `Invoke-SaveRun.ps1` (`Set-Mods`).

### Menu settle
**Id:** blk-480a83d50352  
**Definition**: the four-second wait between the main menu appearing and the load starting. Loading straight from `MainMenu.OnSpawn` threw inside a popup that was still laying out.  
**Used in**: `App_LateUpdate_Patch`.

## Related
**Id:** blk-a61962c63d5a

- See also: [entities](entities.md)

# SaveRunner

## What this is
**Id:** blk-da4886ca7cad

SaveRunner is a development mod plus a launcher script that load a save in the real game with nobody at the keyboard, run the colony for a set number of game seconds with every save to disk blocked, record a probe's readings once per game second and quit. The mod author uses it to reproduce a player's report from their save, once with the mod under test and once without it (`-Without <Mod>`), under the real sim and the player's own loadout, and compares the two `probe.csv` files. The mod does nothing unless the game starts with `--saverun=FILE`, so it can stay installed. Version 0.1.0 in `mod_info.yaml`; not for the Workshop. Mod Profile Manager restarts the game on a changed loadout and is left out with `-Without 2854869130,3281716506`.

## Where things are
**Id:** blk-3dee2f4998e2

Files:

- `Mod.cs`: `SaveRunnerMod`, the `UserMod2` entry point. Reads the command line, sets the crash-reporter flags and traces quits.
- `Runner.cs`: `Runner`, the run's options and state, and `Finish`, which writes the status line and quits.
- `Patches.cs`: the Harmony patches on `MainMenu.OnSpawn`, `App.LateUpdate` (loads the save from the menu, timeout watchdog), `Game.OnSpawn`, `SaveLoader.Save` (blocked) and `App.Quit`.
- `RunBehaviour.cs`: `RunBehaviour`, which runs the colony and samples once per game second, and `FridgeProbe`, the `fridges` probe.
- `Invoke-SaveRun.ps1`: the launcher. Copies the save into `runs/<Label>-<stamp>/`, rewrites `mods.json` for the run (`-With`, `-Without`), starts the game through Steam, restores `mods.json` and prints the status.
- `SaveRunner.csproj`: builds the mod through `common/oni-mod.props` and `common/oni-mod.targets`, which deploy it to the local mods folder.
- `mod.yaml`, `mod_info.yaml`: title "Save Runner (dev tool)", static id `Isochronous.SaveRunner`, version 0.1.0, minimum build 744825.
- `README.md`: setup, running, the probes and how it works.
- `runs/`: created by the launcher; one folder per run with the save copy, `probe.csv`, `probe.csv.status` and `Player.log`. Ignored by `common/.gitignore`.
- `.gitattributes`: line-ending and merge rules for this node's `.context/` files.

The `.context/` documents of this node: [domains](domains/README.md) (entities, glossary), [standards](standards/README.md) (code style, error handling, naming conventions), `decisions/` and `retrospectives/`.

# Code Style Guide

## Formatting
**Id:** blk-9a324aa6540e

### Indentation
**Id:** blk-2ac58ee6eb93

- Tabs, one per level, in every `.cs` file (`Mod.cs`, `Patches.cs`, `Runner.cs`, `RunBehaviour.cs`).
- Four spaces in `Invoke-SaveRun.ps1`; two spaces in `SaveRunner.csproj` and the yaml files.

### Braces
**Id:** blk-8de1cb25887c

- Opening brace on its own line (Allman) for namespaces, types, members and multi-line blocks.
- A body of one short statement goes on the next line without braces (`if (!Runner.Active)` followed by `return;` in `Mod.cs`).
- A `switch` case with one short statement stays on one line (`ReadCommandLine` in `Runner.cs`).

### Line Length
**Id:** blk-459605aea8ce

- No limit and no `.editorconfig`. Long log lines wrap before a `+` with the continuation indented one tab (the start-up `Debug.Log` in `Mod.cs`).

## Language and Toolchain
**Id:** blk-545208d8763a

- C# 9 on .NET Framework 4.8 (`common/oni-mod.props`: `LangVersion` 9.0, `TargetFramework` net48), built against the game's own assemblies through `common/oni-mod.targets`.
- `SaveRunner.csproj` imports the props, sets `AssemblyName`, `RootNamespace` and `Version`, then imports the targets. A successful build deploys the mod to `Documents\Klei\OxygenNotIncluded\mods\local\SaveRunner`.
- The tool is a mod (`mod.yaml`, `mod_info.yaml`, `SaveRunnerMod : UserMod2`) plus one PowerShell launcher. PowerShell is run with `pwsh`.
- Namespace blocks, not file-scoped namespaces.

## Layout
**Id:** blk-233f0aed6e04

One concern per file, all in the node root:

| File | Holds |
|------|-------|
| `Mod.cs` | `SaveRunnerMod`: reads the command line at load, sets the crash-reporter flags, traces who quits |
| `Runner.cs` | `Runner`: static command-line state, `ReadCommandLine`, `Finish` |
| `Patches.cs` | the Harmony patch classes |
| `RunBehaviour.cs` | `RunBehaviour` (the per-frame driver) and `FridgeProbe` (the only probe) |
| `Invoke-SaveRun.ps1` | the launcher |

A new probe is a static class beside `FridgeProbe` with a `Sample(int t, StreamWriter writer, bool toLog)` method, a branch in `RunBehaviour.Begin` for its CSV header and one in `RunBehaviour.Sample`, and an entry in the launcher's `-Probe` `ValidateSet`.

## Inert Without the Argument
**Id:** blk-969f0779ab20

Every patch and hook starts with `if (!Runner.Active) return` (or the equivalent). The mod must stay installed and change nothing when the game starts without `--saverun`. `SaveRunnerMod.OnLoad` returns before patching the quit traces when `Runner.Active` is false.

## Harmony Patches
**Id:** blk-fa011f2987f3

- One static class per patched method, with `[HarmonyPatch(typeof(X), "Method")]` or `nameof` when the member is public, and a `Prefix` or `Postfix` inside (`Patches.cs`).
- The overload is pinned by parameter types when the method has several (`SaveLoader.Save(string, bool, bool)`).
- Private members are named by string; a patch that could be missing on another game build is applied by hand inside try/catch (`SaveRunnerMod.TracePatch`).

## Comments
**Id:** blk-9fd4a51454ee

- Types and patch classes get a `///` summary that says what the code is for and, where a bug shaped it, what went wrong: the four-second menu settle in `Patches.cs`, the crash dialog in `Mod.cs`.
- Command-line options are documented in the `///` summary of `Runner`, in the launcher's comment-based help and in `README.md`; change all three together.
- No commented-out code.

## Related
**Id:** blk-41f957f9abf7

- See also: [error handling](error-handling.md)
- See also: [naming conventions](naming-conventions.md)

description: "How SaveRunner ends and reports a run: the four status values, the driver try/catch, optional hooks, crash dialog, launcher throws, mods.json restore and logging"
applies_to:

# Error Handling Conventions

## Principles
**Id:** blk-225bad67d9a6

1. **A run always ends with a status.** Whatever goes wrong inside the game, `Runner.Finish` writes one JSON line to `<out>.status` and quits, so the launcher never waits on a game that has silently given up.
2. **Never write to the player's data.** The save is copied first and every `SaveLoader.Save` is blocked, so a failed run leaves the colony as it was.
3. **Leave a trace.** Anything that ends the process during a run logs its stack; every failure goes to `Player.log` under the `[SaveRunner] ` tag.
4. **Put the machine back.** The launcher restores `mods.json` in a `finally` block, whatever happened.

## Run Status
**Id:** blk-a1742b4823d2

`Runner.Finish(status, detail)` writes `{"status":..., "save":..., "detail":..., "realSeconds":...}` and calls `App.Quit()`. The first call wins (`Runner.Finished`).

| Status | Written by | Meaning |
|--------|-----------|---------|
| `done` | `RunBehaviour.Update` | the game seconds were reached; `detail` is the sample count |
| `timeout` | `App_LateUpdate_Patch` | no end after `--saverun-timeout` real seconds (default 900) |
| `no-save` | `App_LateUpdate_Patch` | the file named by `--saverun` does not exist |
| `runner-error` | `RunBehaviour.Update` | an exception in the per-frame driver; `detail` is the exception |

The launcher prints the status line, the number of probe rows and the run folder when the game has gone. A missing status file prints `(no status file: the run never finished)`.

## Handling Patterns
**Id:** blk-4db51d308caa

### Driver
**Id:** blk-dbdec23d78e3

`RunBehaviour.Update` runs its whole body in one `try`. The `catch` logs a warning, closes the CSV writer and finishes with `runner-error`. The broad catch is deliberate: an unattended run must end, with the reason recorded.

### Fire-and-forget file writes
**Id:** blk-8cfa00557d4c

Writing the status file is wrapped in its own try/catch that logs a warning (`Runner.Finish`); a failed write must not stop the quit.

### Optional hooks
**Id:** blk-c881d85c0855

`SaveRunnerMod.TracePatch` returns with a warning when the target method is missing and catches an exception from `harmony.Patch`. A game update that moves `App.Restart` costs a warning, not the mod.

### Crash dialog
**Id:** blk-07e31aa20eae

`OnLoad` sets `KCrashReporter.ignoreAll = true` and `terminateOnError = false` during a run. The game's crash dialog quits the process when the scene change destroys it, which ended runs without a word; exceptions still reach the log.

### Command line
**Id:** blk-862fa77a8e5f

`Runner.ReadCommandLine` ignores a number it cannot parse or that is not positive and keeps the default; `--saverun-speed` is clamped to 1 to 3. An unknown `--saverun-*` key is ignored.

### The launcher
**Id:** blk-aa64035a160f

`Invoke-SaveRun.ps1` sets `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'` and checks its preconditions with `throw` and a message that names the fix: save not found, game already running, Steam not found, `SaveRunner is not deployed; run: dotnet build tools/SaveRunner -c Release`, local mod folder not found, game not started within 120 s.

- A leftover `mods.json.saverun-backup` means an earlier launcher died: it is copied back over `mods.json` first, with a warning, so the real loadout is never overwritten by a modified one.
- The game process is stopped (`Stop-Process -Force`) 60 s after the status file stops changing and `TimeoutSec + 180` s after launch, and the launcher says which (`killed-after-status`, `killed`).
- The launcher sets no exit code of its own; a `throw` ends it with PowerShell's failure exit code, and a finished run returns 0 whatever the status, so read the printed status line or `probe.csv.status`.

## Logging
**Id:** blk-f7c3dad5aad4

- All lines go through `Debug.Log` or `Debug.LogWarning` with the `Runner.Tag` prefix (`[SaveRunner] `).
- Warnings for problems the run survives; plain log lines for milestones (loading, colony loaded, running, finished, every quit call).
- Probe rows are copied to the log every tenth game second (`t % 10 == 0`) so the log shows the run progressing.

## Anti-Patterns to Avoid
**Id:** blk-1cec34c97303

- Calling `App.Quit()` directly instead of `Runner.Finish`: no status file is written.
- Loading the save from `MainMenu.OnSpawn`: the menu was torn down under a popup still laying out, which threw and opened the crash dialog. The load waits four seconds after the menu appears.
- Patching without the `Runner.Active` guard.
- Pointing the game at the original save; the launcher always copies it to the run folder.

## Related
**Id:** blk-bb6114284811

- See also: [code style](code-style.md)

# Naming Conventions

## Files and Directories
**Id:** blk-9f3b33d81a6e

- C# files are PascalCase and named for the main type they hold: `Mod.cs`, `Runner.cs`, `Patches.cs`, `RunBehaviour.cs`. `Patches.cs` holds every patch class.
- The launcher is `Invoke-SaveRun.ps1`, a PowerShell Verb-Noun name.
- The mod's folder, assembly (`SaveRunner`) and deployed folder (`mods\local\SaveRunner`) share one name. `mod.yaml` carries `staticID: "Isochronous.SaveRunner"`; the title is "Save Runner (dev tool)".
- Run output lives in `runs/<Label>-<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>/` (ignored by `common/.gitignore`): `colony.sav`, `probe.csv`, `probe.csv.status`, `Player.log`.

## Code Naming
**Id:** blk-4cf0ed5fa17e

- Namespace `SaveRunner`; types PascalCase; locals and parameters camelCase; private fields camelCase with no prefix (`elapsed`, `samples`, `writer`).
- The mod class is `<Tool>Mod : UserMod2` (`SaveRunnerMod`).
- Patch classes are `<Type>_<Method>_Patch` (`MainMenu_OnSpawn_Patch`, `SaveLoader_Save_Patch`, `App_LateUpdate_Patch`), with methods named `Prefix` or `Postfix`.
- Run state is public static fields on `Runner` named for what they hold (`SavePath`, `Seconds`, `Speed`, `Probe`, `OutFile`, `TimeoutSeconds`); flags are `Active`, `Started`, `Finished`; times with a real-time meaning end in `At` (`StartedAt`, `MenuSeenAt`).
- A probe is a static class named `<Subject>Probe` (`FridgeProbe`) with a `Sample` method; the probe's name on the command line is the subject in lower case (`fridges`).
- Log tag: `Runner.Tag`, the string `[SaveRunner] `.

## Command Line and Launcher
**Id:** blk-5068e4f0855f

- Game arguments are `--saverun` followed by `-<option>`, lower case, hyphen-separated, as `--saverun-seconds=N`. `--saverun=FILE` itself names the save. `Runner` reads `--key=value` and a bare `--key` as an empty value.
- Launcher parameters are PowerShell PascalCase (`-Seconds`, `-Speed`, `-Probe`, `-With`, `-Without`, `-TimeoutSec`, `-Label`, `-OutDir`, `-SteamExe`, `-AppId`). `-Seconds`, `-Speed`, `-Probe` and `-TimeoutSec` map straight to `--saverun-seconds`, `--saverun-speed`, `--saverun-probe` and `--saverun-timeout`. `-Save` becomes `--saverun=<copy of the save in the run folder>`, and the run folder, named from `-OutDir` and `-Label`, gives `--saverun-out=<run folder>/probe.csv`. `-With`, `-Without`, `-SteamExe` and `-AppId` configure only the launcher: the loadout, the Steam path and the app to launch.
- `-With` and `-Without` take local mod folder names or Workshop item ids, comma-separated.
- Probe names are lower case plurals of the thing sampled (`fridges`).

## CSV Columns
**Id:** blk-885a11539bd3

Header names are camelCase with units spelled in the name (`setpointC`, `cellTempC`, `massKg`, `deltaKJ`), sample time first as `t`. Each game second writes one row per item in a fridge, or one row for a fridge with no items.

## Related
**Id:** blk-8e408dfe956d

- See also: [code style](code-style.md)

description: "TestRunner's real things: the harness mod, Session, TestBehaviour, patches, FixtureArea, Worldgen, Reflect, the test kit, the launcher and warden, files, rules and states"

# TestRunner domain

## Overview
**Id:** blk-70f176589bcc

TestRunner runs a mod's in-game tests in the real game with nobody at the keyboard. A launcher builds the mod's test project, checks it with ModCheck, starts the game with `--onitest-dir=DIR --onitest-save=FILE`, and the harness mod loads a fixture save, runs every `[OniTest]` coroutine found in `DIR/tests/*.dll`, writes one JSON line per test and a status line, and quits (or stays up for the next run). Tests drive the game the way a player does: the real `InterfaceTool` fed the calls the player controller makes (layer 1), with the game's own API for setup and oracles (layer 0). It is a development tool, not for the Workshop, and inert without its arguments. The user-facing guide is `README.md`.

## Key Entities
**Id:** blk-978685bb1f6f

### TestRunnerMod
**Id:** blk-12154230c41b  
**Description**: the entry point (`UserMod2`). Reads the command line, sets the crash-reporter flags, adds the assembly resolver that lets test assemblies find the mods under test and this harness, and traces quits.  
**Location**: `Mod.cs`  
**Relationships**: calls `Session.ReadCommandLine`; the patches in `Patches.cs`, `Worldgen.cs` and `Diagnostics.cs` are applied by `base.OnLoad`.

### Session
**Id:** blk-7f9302c43486  
**Description**: command line, state and results of a session.  
**Location**: `Session.cs`

| Member | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `Active`, `Started`, `Finished` | session flags; `Active` needs `--onitest-dir` and `--onitest-save` |
| `Dir`, `SavePath`, `Filters`, `TimeoutSeconds`, `TestTimeoutSeconds`, `Keep`, `Trace`, `ServerDir` | the options |
| `Tests`, `NextIndex` | the selected tests and the next to run; survive a scene change |
| `Passed`, `Failed`, `Errors`, `Timeouts`, `Skipped`, `Reloads` | counters for the status line |
| `Discover()` | loads every DLL in `DIR/tests` from its bytes and lists `[OniTest]` methods, sorted by assembly, class and declaration order |
| `Start()`, `Continue()`, `WriteOff()` | begin a run; move to the next test's world or fixture; record tests as not run |
| `Write(result)`, `Finish(status, detail)` | append a result; write the status and quit or go idle |
| `PollQueue()`, `WriteState()` | live-session requests and state file |

### TestCase and TestResult
**Id:** blk-18187e3cb8c6  
**Description**: a discovered test method (id, name, timeout, layer and the attribute flags) and what one test produced (one `results.jsonl` line).  
**Location**: `Session.cs`

### TestBehaviour
**Id:** blk-49587b759cd2  
**Description**: a `MonoBehaviour` on the Game object (or on a driver object for a no-colony run). Waits for the HUD, throws the harness switches, finds and clears the fixture area, then runs each test as a hand-stepped coroutine with a real-time deadline, captures logged errors, runs cleanups and writes the result.  
**Location**: `TestBehaviour.cs` (`LogCapture` in the same file)

### Patches
**Id:** blk-6e02b4b02569  
**Description**: Harmony patches, each inert unless `Session.Active`.  
**Location**: `Patches.cs`

| Patch | Does |
|-------|------|
| `MainMenu_OnSpawn_Patch` | notes when the menu appeared |
| `App_LateUpdate_Patch` | four seconds after the menu: starts the session; drives worldgen; session timeout; polls the live queue |
| `Game_OnSpawn_Patch` | adds `TestBehaviour` when the colony is up |
| `SaveLoader_Save_Patch`, `Game_StartDelayedSave_Patch` | block saves outside the run folder; skip autosave |
| `App_Quit_Patch` | logs who quit |
| `Manager_MatchFootprint_Patch`, `Manager_Report_Patch` | no "mod differences" or "mod events" dialogs |
| `GameFlowManager_CheckForGameOver_Patch` | no "colony lost" screen on a fixture with no Duplicants |
| `KInputManager_OnApplicationFocus_Patch`, `InterfaceTool_OnApplicationFocus_Patch` | force the focus flags back on |

### Harness
**Id:** blk-052ae0295b17  
**Description**: the global switches of a run: focus forced on, mouse position locked (parked in the bottom right corner between tests), physical keyboard and mouse ignored, instant build on, speed 1, tool reset, camera look-at.  
**Location**: `Harness.cs`

### FixtureArea
**Id:** blk-633dd6387bca  
**Description**: the 40 by 10 rectangle of the active world that tests build in: fully revealed and buildable, with the most empty cells (cells underground count double). Cleared before the first test and after every test (objects, loose items, solid cells; Duplicants are the test's to remove). `Dupes.Box` walls it for Duplicant tests.  
**Location**: `FixtureArea.cs`

### Worldgen and GeneratedWorld
**Id:** blk-9e3323c536e4  
**Description**: tests marked `[OniTest(Worldgen = "COORD")]` run in a world freshly generated from that coordinate: the harness goes to the main menu, applies the coordinate, runs the game's worldgen screen, embarks, then runs the test. Consecutive tests with one coordinate share the world. `GeneratedWorld` records the coordinate, the applied coordinate, the cluster, worldgen errors and seconds.  
**Location**: `Worldgen.cs`

### Reflect and Diagnostics
**Id:** blk-741c81a8a7c1

**Description**: `Reflect` is the list of private game members the kit and tests use, with `SelfCheck`; `Worldgen.cs` reads two buttons with its own `AccessTools.Field` calls. `Diagnostics` traces the grid marks the game makes during tests (`--onitest-trace=1`).  
**Location**: `Reflect.cs`, `Diagnostics.cs`

### The kit (`Isochronous.TestKit`)
**Id:** blk-c6e1619a47bb  
**Description**: what a test author uses.  
**Location**: `Kit/`

| Type | File | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `OniTestAttribute`, `LayerAttribute` | `Attributes.cs` | mark tests and set their options (`Timeout`, `FreshSave`, `Explicit`, `Boxed`, `NoColony`, `Worldgen`) |
| `OniAssertException`, `SkipException` | `Attributes.cs` | thrown by `t.Assert` and `t.Skip` |
| `TestContext` | `TestContext.cs` | `Assert`, `World`, `Tools`, `Dupes`, waits (`Frames`, `WaitGameSeconds`, `WaitRealSeconds`, `WaitUntil`), `Rect`, `Area`, `Log`, `Cleanup`, `AllowLogError`, `Skip`, `Speed`, `InstantBuild`, `ResearchAll`, `Screenshot`, `Press`, `PointAt`, `LookAt`, `Generated` |
| `Wait` and its subclasses, `CellRect` | `TestContext.cs` | what a test yields; a rectangle of cells |
| `OniAssert` | `OniAssert.cs` | `True`, `False`, `Eq`, `NotEq`, `Null`, `NotNull`, `Has`, `Lacks`, `Fail` |
| `World`, `Cells` | `World.cs` | `Build`, `At`, `Destroy`, `LogicNetwork`, `LogicConnections` at layer 0; cell descriptions |
| `Tools`, `UtilityDragSession` | `Tools.cs` | the real utility build tool at layer 1: `Path`, `Sweep`, `PreviewTint`, `PreviewValid` |
| `Dupes` | `Dupes.cs` | `Box`, `ClearBox`, `Spawn`, `Grant`, `GrantAll`, `Drop`, `Remove`, `RemoveAll` |
| `SaveFile` | `SaveFile.cs` | `Capture` and `Restore` a building through the game's own save and load |

### Invoke-OniTests.ps1
**Id:** blk-5b0c52216ccc  
**Description**: the launcher. For each mod in `-Mods`, finds `src/<Mod>.Tests/<Mod>.Tests.csproj` (in a repo or under `mods/`), builds it, checks the test DLL with `tools/ModCheck`, copies it into the run folder, rewrites `mods.json` so only TestRunner, the mods under test, `-With` and `-Steam` are enabled, launches the game through Steam (or hands the run to a live game), waits for the status, prints a line per test and exits with its code.  
**Location**: `Invoke-OniTests.ps1`  
**Options**: `-Mods` (required), `-Filter`, `-Fixture`, `-With`, `-Steam`, `-TimeoutSec`, `-TestTimeoutSec`, `-KeepGame`, `-BuildOnly`, `-NoBuild`, `-NoCheck`, `-BuildArgs`, `-Label`, `-Trace`, `-OutDir`, `-SteamExe`, `-AppId`.

### Watch-OniGame.ps1
**Id:** blk-5f4f98f50aec  
**Description**: the warden of a live session, started detached next to the game. Waits for the game to exit, restores `mods.json` from the backup, removes the live-session folder; ends a game that stops answering.  
**Location**: `Watch-OniGame.ps1`

### Files
**Id:** blk-aabf5834e2e4

| File | Direction | Purpose |
|------|-----------|---------|
| `DIR/tests/*.dll` | read | the test assemblies |
| `DIR/results.jsonl`, `results.jsonl.status` | written by the game | per-test results; the session status |
| `DIR/artifacts/*.png` | written by the game | `t.Screenshot` output |
| fixture save | read | copied to the run folder as `fixture.sav`; never written back |
| `Documents\Klei\OxygenNotIncluded\mods\mods.json` | rewritten, restored | the run's loadout; backup `mods.json.onitest-backup` |
| `%LOCALAPPDATA%\IsochronousOniTests\live` | read, written | live-session queue, state and pid |

## Business Rules
**Id:** blk-ad9c4a3b39af

- Without `--onitest-dir` and `--onitest-save` the mod changes nothing.
- No save goes to disk outside the run folder, and the game's autosave is skipped.
- A test is `public static IEnumerator M(TestContext t)` with `[OniTest]`; any other signature with the attribute fails the session at discovery.
- Tests run in order of assembly name, class, declaration. An `Explicit` test runs only when `-Filter` selects it.
- Any `Error`, `Exception` or `Assert` the game logs during a test fails it unless `t.AllowLogError` allows it.
- Each mod's tests start on a fresh load of the fixture; `[OniTest(FreshSave = true)]` loads it again before a test, after a settle of five game seconds.
- A run is handed to a live game only when the loadout matches: the mode, the mods, `-With`, `-Steam`, `-Trace` and every file of each deployed local mod, the harness and their shared configs. Anything else ends the game and launches a new one.
- The game stays up 15 s after a run for another; one run at a time per machine.
- A world coordinate of the other game mode skips its tests.
- A run needs Steam running and the game not running (apart from its own live session).

## Key Code Paths
**Id:** blk-8a2f716a53ff

- **Launch**: `Invoke-OniTests.ps1` builds, runs ModCheck, writes `mods.json`, starts or hands over to the game. See `Invoke-OniTests.ps1`.
- **Start**: `MainMenu.OnSpawn` postfix, then `App.LateUpdate` postfix calls `Session.Start`: `Discover`, then `Continue` loads the fixture (`LoadScreen.DoLoad`) or asks for a world. See `Patches.cs`, `Session.cs`.
- **Run**: `Game.OnSpawn` postfix adds `TestBehaviour`; `RunAll` picks the area, clears it and steps each test with `RunOne`. See `TestBehaviour.cs`.
- **Generated world**: `Worldgen.Begin` at the main menu, `Worldgen.Embark` after the colony spawns. See `Worldgen.cs`.
- **End**: `Session.Finish` writes the status and quits or goes idle; the launcher reads `results.jsonl` and the status and exits. See `Session.cs`, `Invoke-OniTests.ps1`.
- **Live session**: `Session.PollQueue` takes `<run>.req`, `Session.Begin` resets and starts again. See `Session.cs`.

## State Transitions
**Id:** blk-27f068ae61ee

| State | Transitions To | Trigger |
|-------|---------------|---------|
| test pending | pass, fail, error, timeout, skipped | the driver steps it (see [error handling](../standards/error-handling.md)) |
| session busy | idle | `Session.Finish` in a live session |
| session idle | busy | a request in `queue` |
| session idle | quitting | `quit.req`, or 15 s with no request |

## Related
**Id:** blk-ac2e0e4164d8

- See also: [glossary](glossary.md)
- Governed by: [naming conventions](../standards/naming-conventions.md)

# TestRunner glossary

Terms a newcomer to TestRunner needs. Entity detail is in [entities](entities.md).

## Abbreviations and Acronyms
**Id:** blk-f88dca2a1b27

| Abbreviation | Full Term | Context |
|--------------|-----------|---------|
| ONI | Oxygen Not Included | the game |
| SO | Spaced Out | the expansion; its mode loads `testbed-so.sav`, the only fixture supplied |
| HUD | heads-up display | the driver waits up to 60 s for it before the first test |
| DLL | test assembly | `<Mod>.Tests.dll`, copied to `DIR/tests` |

## Cross-Domain Terms
**Id:** blk-d5cc7906d14d

### Harness
**Id:** blk-0c81d2ef6d47  
**Definition**: the TestRunner mod itself: the code in the game that loads the fixture, steps tests and reports. Versus the kit, which is what tests call.  
**Used in**: `Harness.cs`, `README.md`.

### Kit
**Id:** blk-cddba398d1da  
**Definition**: `Isochronous.TestKit` in `Kit/`: the test context, assertions, attributes and helpers a test project references.  
**Used in**: every test project.

### Fixture
**Id:** blk-4199508c4e2e

**Definition**: the save a run loads: `fixtures/testbed-so.sav` in Spaced Out mode (the only fixture supplied), `fixtures/testbed-base.sav` in base-game mode (copy it in first), or the `-Fixture` path: sandbox on, no Duplicants, revealed map. Tests never change the file; the launcher copies it into the run folder.  
**Used in**: `Session.Continue`, the launcher.

### Fixture area
**Id:** blk-a0cfe36dee6e  
**Definition**: the 40 by 10 window of the active world that the harness picks and clears for tests (`FixtureArea`); `t.Rect(w, h)` gives a clear rectangle inside it with a one-cell margin.  
**Used in**: `FixtureArea.cs`, `TestContext`.

### Layer
**Id:** blk-46885449ff2a  
**Definition**: where a test drives the game: 0 the game's API, 1 the tool (real `InterfaceTool` input), 2 UI, 3 input. Recorded with `[Layer(n)]` and in the results; layers 2 and 3 are not built.  
**Used in**: `LayerAttribute`, `TestResult`.

### Run, session and live session
**Id:** blk-be133b9156d5  
**Definition**: a run is one launcher invocation's tests. A session is one game process taking runs. A live session is a game that stays up 15 s after a run and takes the next one with the same loadout from its queue.  
**Used in**: `Session.cs`, the launcher, `Watch-OniGame.ps1`.

### Warden
**Id:** blk-17051b9bdfa7  
**Definition**: `Watch-OniGame.ps1`, the detached process that restores `mods.json` and clears the live-session folder when the game exits.  
**Used in**: the launcher, `Watch-OniGame.ps1`.

### Wait
**Id:** blk-12fc1ae73c38  
**Definition**: an object a test yields (`t.Frames`, `t.WaitGameSeconds`, `t.WaitRealSeconds`, `t.WaitUntil`); the driver polls it once per frame against the test's deadline and fails the test with its description when it times out.  
**Used in**: `Kit/TestContext.cs`, `TestBehaviour.cs`.

### Box
**Id:** blk-40af48693237  
**Definition**: the Duplicants' box: tiles walling the fixture area with air inside and a dev life support, made by `t.Dupes.Box()`; `[OniTest(Boxed = true)]` keeps it between consecutive tests.  
**Used in**: `Kit/Dupes.cs`, `FixtureArea.cs`.

### Loadout
**Id:** blk-90066b0e7a52  
**Definition**: the list of enabled mods in `mods.json`. A run enables only TestRunner, the mods under test, `-With` and `-Steam`; the player's is backed up and restored.  
**Used in**: the launcher, the warden.

### Generated world
**Id:** blk-4d6d5f72d7c2  
**Definition**: a world made fresh from a coordinate such as `SNDST-C-100-0-0-0` (the letter before the seed is `C` for Spaced Out, `A` for base game) for tests with `Worldgen = ...`.  
**Used in**: `Worldgen.cs`.

### Self-check
**Id:** blk-14e9c9072d5c  
**Definition**: `Reflect.SelfCheck()`, run before the first test, listing the private game members that no longer resolve.  
**Used in**: `Reflect.cs`.

## Related
**Id:** blk-db910f4597a3

- See also: [entities](entities.md)

# TestRunner

## What this is
**Id:** blk-666b8641eaaa

TestRunner runs an Oxygen Not Included mod's in-game tests in the real game with nobody at the keyboard. It has two halves. The harness is a development-only mod (`Isochronous.TestRunner`, version 0.1.0 in `mod_info.yaml`, minimum build 744825, not for the Workshop): started with `--onitest-dir=DIR --onitest-save=FILE`, it loads a fixture save, blocks saves outside `DIR`, runs every `[OniTest]` coroutine in `DIR/tests/*.dll`, writes one JSON line per test and a status line, then quits or stays up 15 s for the next run. The launcher, `Invoke-OniTests.ps1`, builds a mod's `<Mod>.Tests` project, checks it with `tools/ModCheck`, sets the enabled mods in `mods.json`, starts the game through Steam (or hands the run to a game already up with the same loadout) and prints a line per test. Tests compile against the test kit, `Isochronous.TestKit` in `Kit/`, and drive the game the way a player does. Without its arguments the mod does nothing, so it stays installed. The mod developer and the agents working on ONI-Mods use it: every mod's `src/<ModName>.Tests/` project runs through it.

## Where things are
**Id:** blk-b5f287049a7f

Top-level folders and key files:

- `Mod.cs`: the `UserMod2` entry point. Reads the command line, turns the crash dialog off for a run and resolves test assemblies against the mods under test.
- `Session.cs`: the options, the discovered tests, the counters, the results and status files, and the live-session queue.
- `TestBehaviour.cs`: steps each test's coroutine by hand with a real-time deadline, captures errors the game logs and runs cleanups.
- `Patches.cs`: the Harmony patches that start a run from the main menu, block saves outside the run folder, skip autosave, suppress the mod and game-over dialogs and force the focus flags.
- `Harness.cs`: the run-wide switches: focus forced on, mouse locked, physical keyboard and mouse ignored, instant build, speed 1.
- `FixtureArea.cs`: picks the 40x10 test area in the fixture world and clears it before and after each test.
- `Worldgen.cs`: runs `[OniTest(Worldgen = ...)]` tests in a world freshly generated from a coordinate.
- `Reflect.cs`: every private game member the harness and kit read, with the self-check; `Diagnostics.cs`: the grid-mark trace behind `-Trace`.
- `Kit/`: the test kit (`Attributes.cs`, `TestContext.cs`, `OniAssert.cs`, `World.cs`, `Tools.cs`, `Dupes.cs`, `SaveFile.cs`).
- `Invoke-OniTests.ps1`: the launcher. `Watch-OniGame.ps1`: the warden that puts `mods.json` back and removes the live-session folder after the game exits.
- `fixtures/`: `testbed-so.sav`, the Spaced Out fixture save and the only test save tracked in git, and `README.md` on what makes a good fixture. The base-game fixture the launcher looks for, `testbed-base.sav`, is not in the repo.
- `TestRunner.csproj`: imports `oni-mod.props` and `oni-mod.targets` from the root of common; `mod.yaml` and `mod_info.yaml` beside it.
- `README.md`: running the launcher and its options, writing tests, the output and how it works.
- `runs/`: one folder per run (`<label>-<stamp>`) with the results, `Player.log`, the fixture copy and the checked DLLs; ignored by git.

The `.context/` documents of this node: [domains](domains/README.md) (entities, glossary), [standards](standards/README.md) (code style, error handling, naming conventions), `decisions/` and `retrospectives/`.

# Code Style Guide

## Formatting
**Id:** blk-a5a05cca59dd

### Indentation
**Id:** blk-48bf49a3a8d9

- Tabs, one per level, in every `.cs` file, including `Kit/`.
- Four spaces in `Invoke-OniTests.ps1` and `Watch-OniGame.ps1`; two spaces in `TestRunner.csproj` and the yaml files.

### Braces
**Id:** blk-d5d494815e7f

- Opening brace on its own line (Allman) for namespaces, types, members and multi-line blocks.
- A body of one short statement goes on the next line without braces (`if (!Session.Active)` followed by `return;` in `Mod.cs`).
- A `switch` case with one short statement stays on one line (`Session.ReadCommandLine`).

### Line Length
**Id:** blk-c5dee5000810

- No limit and no `.editorconfig`. Long log lines wrap before a `+` with the continuation indented one tab (the start-up `Debug.Log` in `Mod.cs`).

## Language and Toolchain
**Id:** blk-827b53b95cbe

- C# 9 on .NET Framework 4.8, built against the game's assemblies (`common/oni-mod.props` and `oni-mod.targets`). `TestRunner.csproj` sets `ReferenceUnityUI` and references `UnityEngine.ScreenCaptureModule` for `t.Screenshot`.
- The tool is a mod (`mod.yaml`, `mod_info.yaml`, `TestRunnerMod : UserMod2`) and also a library: a mod's test project references `TestRunner.csproj` for the kit. A successful build deploys it to `Documents\Klei\OxygenNotIncluded\mods\local\TestRunner`.
- Two namespaces: `Isochronous.TestRunner` for the harness (the code that runs a session) and `Isochronous.TestKit` for what a test author uses (`Kit/`: the test context, assertions, attributes, dupes, tools, world helpers). Harness types a test may touch are public; the rest is `internal`.
- Namespace blocks, not file-scoped namespaces. PowerShell is run with `pwsh`.

## Layout
**Id:** blk-3eafd0a33a08

| Path | Holds |
|------|-------|
| `Mod.cs` | `TestRunnerMod`: command line at load, crash-reporter flags, assembly resolve, quit tracing |
| `Session.cs` | `Session` (command line, test discovery, results, live-session queue), `TestCase`, `TestResult`, `Json` |
| `TestBehaviour.cs` | the driver that steps each test, `LogCapture` |
| `Patches.cs` | the Harmony patches |
| `Harness.cs` | the global switches a run throws |
| `FixtureArea.cs` | choosing and clearing the test area |
| `Worldgen.cs` | tests in a generated world |
| `Reflect.cs` | the private game members the kit and tests touch |
| `Diagnostics.cs` | opt-in grid-mark tracing |
| `Kit/` | the test kit |
| `Invoke-OniTests.ps1`, `Watch-OniGame.ps1` | launcher and warden |
| `fixtures/` | fixture saves and their README |

## Inert Without the Argument
**Id:** blk-2fc671d7925c

Every patch starts with `if (!Session.Active) ...`. `Session.Active` is true only with both `--onitest-dir` and `--onitest-save`. The mod stays installed and changes nothing in a normal game session.

## Harmony Patches
**Id:** blk-bb5bf3709593

- One static class per patched method, named `<Type>_<Method>_Patch`, with `Prefix` or `Postfix` (`Patches.cs`); trace patches in `Diagnostics.cs` are named `_Trace`.
- Overloads are pinned by parameter types (`BuildingDef.TryPlace` in `Diagnostics.cs`).
- A patch that might not exist on another game build is applied by hand in try/catch (`TestRunnerMod.TracePatch`).

## Private Game Members
**Id:** blk-7ca12f96cdb9

The kit and the tests reach game internals only through `Reflect.cs`: a `public static readonly FieldInfo` per member from `AccessTools`, with a `///` summary saying what it is for, and a line in `Reflect.SelfCheck()`. `FieldInfo` is used and `FieldRefAccess` is not, because a `FieldRef` dynamic method cannot be built on the CoreCLR host that ModCheck runs on.

The harness has two exceptions. `Worldgen.cs` reads `CharacterSelectionController.proceedButton` and `WattsonMessage.button` with its own `AccessTools.Field` calls (`ProceedButton`, `WattsonButton`), and `SelfCheck` does not list them. `Mod.cs` resolves `App.Restart` and `Application.Quit` with `AccessTools.Method` for the quit trace, applied by hand through `TracePatch`. TODO(owner): move the two `Worldgen.cs` fields into `Reflect.cs` and `SelfCheck`.

## Comments
**Id:** blk-2536019dd87f

- Types, patches and switches get a `///` summary giving the purpose and, where a failure shaped the code, what failed (the settle before a reload in `TestBehaviour`, the focus patches in `Patches.cs`).
- Options are documented in three places that change together: the `///` summary of `Session`, the launcher's comment-based help and `README.md`.
- Kit members that a test author calls carry a summary written for that author.
- No commented-out code.

## Related
**Id:** blk-657b3eb1a17f

- See also: [error handling](error-handling.md)
- See also: [naming conventions](naming-conventions.md)

# Error Handling Conventions

## Principles
**Id:** blk-23a64c67c430

1. **A session always ends with a status.** `Session.Finish` writes `results.jsonl.status` whatever happened, so the launcher never waits on a game that has silently given up.
2. **A test never takes the run down.** Each test's exception, timeout or logged error becomes that test's result and the next test runs.
3. **Never write to the player's data.** Saving is blocked outside the run folder, and the launcher backs up and restores `mods.json`.
4. **Leave a trace.** Whatever ends the process during a session logs its stack; everything goes to `Player.log` under the `[TestRunner] ` tag and into the run folder.
5. **A renamed game member names itself.** `Reflect.SelfCheck` fails the run with the member's name before the first test.

## Test Results
**Id:** blk-5d3610d2392d

One JSON line per test in `results.jsonl`. The driver steps each test by hand (`RunOne` in `TestBehaviour.cs`) inside try/catch and `Classify` maps what it caught:

| Status | Cause |
|--------|-------|
| `pass` | the test ended with no exception and the game logged no error |
| `fail` | `OniAssertException` from `t.Assert`; a `Wait` that timed out (`timed out waiting for ...`); an `Error`, `Exception` or `Assert` the game logged during the test and `t.AllowLogError` did not allow |
| `error` | any other exception (`Type: message` and the stack) |
| `timeout` | the test's real-time deadline passed (`[OniTest(Timeout = n)]`, else `--onitest-test-timeout`) |
| `skipped` | `t.Skip(reason)`, or a `Worldgen` coordinate of the other mode |

Cleanups registered with `t.Cleanup` run after every test, in reverse order; one that throws is recorded in the result's notes and the others still run. `Harness.ResetTools` and `ParkMouse` run after every test.

## Session Status
**Id:** blk-a16ba6352e62

`Session.Finish(status, detail)` writes one JSON line with the counts and quits (unless `--onitest-keep`, or a live session, which goes idle).

| Status | Written by | Meaning |
|--------|-----------|---------|
| `done` | `Session`, `TestBehaviour` | every selected test ran; `detail` is the summary |
| `runner-error` | `Session.Start`, `TestBehaviour` | test discovery failed, the HUD did not appear within 60 s, or the driver threw |
| `no-save` | `Session.Continue` | the fixture file does not exist |
| `timeout` | `App_LateUpdate_Patch` | no end after `--onitest-timeout` real seconds (default 600) |
| `worldgen-hang` | `Worldgen.Watch` | no worldgen progress for 300 s |

A failed world generation is not a session failure: its tests are written off as `fail` (`Session.WriteOff`) and the run goes on.

## Launcher Exit Codes
**Id:** blk-8aed4db67098

`Invoke-OniTests.ps1` ends with:

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | session status `done` and every test passed |
| 1 | a test failed, errored or timed out, or no test ran |
| 2 | the session produced no status, or a status other than `done` (launch, load or crash: read `Player.log` in the run folder) |
| 3 | the build or the ModCheck pass failed |

Preconditions use `throw` with a message that names the fix: game already running, Steam not found, fixture not found, fixture of the wrong mode, test project not found, mod not deployed, Workshop mod not installed, local mod folder not found, game did not start within 120 s.

## Handling Patterns
**Id:** blk-0a556e7a86fb

### Hand-stepped coroutines
**Id:** blk-ee72d04f56e6

`TestBehaviour.Guarded` and `RunOne` call `MoveNext` themselves inside try/catch. An exception inside a Unity-driven coroutine cannot be caught by its starter and a timeout cannot stop it. The real-time deadline is checked at every step.

### Driver failures
**Id:** blk-1fbd16bb06a4

An exception the driver did not expect ends the session at once as `runner-error` with the exception, never as an idle game waiting for the session timeout.

### Side files
**Id:** blk-a0ed021080ba

Writing a result, the status file or the session state is wrapped in try/catch that logs a warning (`Session.Write`, `Session.Finish`, `Session.WriteState`); a failed write must not stop the run.

### Crash dialog
**Id:** blk-ed7fda19418a

`OnLoad` sets `KCrashReporter.ignoreAll = true` and `terminateOnError = false`. The game's crash dialog quits the process when the scene change destroys it, which ended runs without a word; exceptions still reach the log.

### Mods.json and the warden
**Id:** blk-73f72ee0a0b7

The launcher copies `mods.json` to `mods.json.onitest-backup` before changing it. A leftover backup means an earlier launcher or warden died; the next run restores it first. `Watch-OniGame.ps1` puts the file back and removes the live-session folder once the game has exited; it ends a game that has been idle in its state file for over a minute, or busy three minutes past its own deadline.

### One run at a time
**Id:** blk-040f34128326

The launcher takes the machine-wide mutex `Global\IsochronousOniTests` and says "waiting for it to finish" when another run holds it. An abandoned mutex is taken over.

## Logging
**Id:** blk-54e6d79709fb

- All harness lines use `Session.Tag` (`[TestRunner] `) through `Debug.Log` or `Debug.LogWarning`.
- `t.Log(text)` writes to the result's notes and to `Player.log` as `[TestRunner] <test id>: <text>`.
- Test code reports failures with `t.Assert.*` and its message argument, which names what was expected; `t.WaitUntil(cond, timeout, what)` fails with `what`.

## Anti-Patterns to Avoid
**Id:** blk-8ac04f4e983a

- Calling `App.Quit()` directly instead of `Session.Finish`: no status is written.
- Reading a private game member by a bare `AccessTools` call in a test or kit file; it goes in `Reflect.cs` with a self-check.
- A test that builds, changes and clears frames apart; the game's sim callbacks arrive after the objects are gone. Wait game time between steps.
- An `Error` logged during a test that is expected (a game warning path): allow it with `t.AllowLogError(regex)`, do not loosen the check.
- Starting a run with the game open: the launcher refuses, except for its own live session.

## Related
**Id:** blk-4d93c98455cc

- See also: [code style](code-style.md)

# Naming Conventions

## Files and Directories
**Id:** blk-dbf5ebc0be89

- C# files are PascalCase and named for the main type they hold (`Session.cs`, `Harness.cs`, `FixtureArea.cs`). `Patches.cs` holds every patch class; `Kit/` holds one file per kit area (`Dupes.cs`, `Tools.cs`, `World.cs`, `OniAssert.cs`, `TestContext.cs`, `Attributes.cs`, `SaveFile.cs`).
- Scripts use PowerShell Verb-Noun names: `Invoke-OniTests.ps1`, `Watch-OniGame.ps1`.
- The mod's folder, assembly (`TestRunner`) and deployed folder share one name. `mod.yaml` carries `staticID: "Isochronous.TestRunner"`; the title is "Test Runner (dev tool)".
- The launcher picks the fixture by the game's current mode: `fixtures/testbed-so.sav` for Spaced Out, `fixtures/testbed-base.sav` for base game. Only `testbed-so.sav` is supplied (it is tracked in common). A base-game run needs `testbed-base.sav` copied into `fixtures/` or a `-Fixture <path>` argument; without one the launcher throws `Fixture save not found`.
- Run folders are `runs/<label>-<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>/` (ignored by `common/.gitignore`) holding `tests/`, `check/<Mod>/`, `fixture.sav`, `results.jsonl`, `results.jsonl.status`, `summary.txt`, `Player.log`, `mods.json.used`, `mods.json.real` and `artifacts/`. The label is short and names the work (`bs-cleanup`, `bs-bao`).
- The live session folder is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\IsochronousOniTests\live` (with `queue`, `state`, `game.pid`); the warden's log sits next to it.
- A mod's test project is `src/<Mod>.Tests/<Mod>.Tests.csproj`; its assembly is `<Mod>.Tests`.

## Code Naming
**Id:** blk-81d3dab6af5e

- Namespaces `Isochronous.TestRunner` (harness) and `Isochronous.TestKit` (kit).
- Types PascalCase, locals and parameters camelCase, private fields camelCase with no prefix. The harness's state lives in public static fields of static classes named for the concern (`Session`, `Harness`, `FixtureArea`, `Worldgen`, `Reflect`).
- The mod class is `TestRunnerMod : UserMod2`; the driver is `TestBehaviour`.
- Patch classes are `<Type>_<Method>_Patch`; trace patches end in `_Trace`.
- Reflection handles in `Reflect` are named `<Type><Member>` (`KInputManagerHasFocus`, `InterfaceToolIsAppFocused`, `PathNodeCell`); the self-check message uses the game's own `Type.member`.
- Waits are classes ending in `Wait` deriving from `Wait` (`FrameWait`, `GameSecondsWait`, `UntilWait`); the `TestContext` factory methods that make them are `Frames`, `WaitGameSeconds`, `WaitRealSeconds`, `WaitUntil`.
- Attributes end in `Attribute` and are used without the suffix: `[OniTest]`, `[Layer]`. `OniTest` options are PascalCase properties: `Timeout`, `FreshSave`, `Explicit`, `Boxed`, `NoColony`, `Worldgen`.
- Test classes are `public static` classes named for the area under test (`WireDrags`); test methods are `public static IEnumerator <Name>(TestContext t)` named for what is checked (`DragFromEnd`). The test id is `<Assembly>/<Class>.<Method>`. The attribute's display name starts with a short mod prefix (`"DAB: wire dragged from a bridge end to its neighbour connects both"`).
- Assertion methods are short (`True`, `False`, `Eq`, `NotEq`, `Null`, `NotNull`, `Has`, `Lacks`, `Fail`) and take the message last.

## Command Line and Launcher
**Id:** blk-afb883826043

- Game arguments are `--onitest-<option>=value`, lower case, hyphen-separated: `--onitest-dir`, `--onitest-save`, `--onitest-filter`, `--onitest-timeout`, `--onitest-test-timeout`, `--onitest-keep`, `--onitest-trace`, `--onitest-server`.
- Launcher parameters are PowerShell PascalCase (`-Mods`, `-Filter`, `-Fixture`, `-With`, `-Steam`, `-TimeoutSec`, `-TestTimeoutSec`, `-KeepGame`, `-BuildOnly`, `-NoBuild`, `-NoCheck`, `-BuildArgs`, `-Label`, `-Trace`).
- `-Filter` is one word with no spaces (it travels through Steam's command line); globs use `*` and `?`, several separated by `;`.
- Run folder paths contain no spaces for the same reason.
- Live-session request files are `<run>.req` with `key=value` lines, renamed `.taken` when the game takes them; `quit.req` ends the session.

## Results
**Id:** blk-982a2140c0af

`results.jsonl` fields are lower camel case: `id`, `assembly`, `class`, `method`, `name`, `layer`, `status`, `message`, `stack`, `durationSeconds`, `gameSeconds`, `logErrors`, `notes`. Statuses are lower case words: `pass`, `fail`, `error`, `timeout`, `skipped`. Screenshots are `artifacts/<Assembly>.<Class>.<Method>-<name>.png`.

## Related
**Id:** blk-86f3ccc4f182

- See also: [code style](code-style.md)
